Q116442752.label: 2025 Jamaican general election
Q116442752.summary: General elections were held in Jamaica on 3 September 2025. The incumbent Jamaica Labour Party (JLP) government, led by Prime Minister Andrew Holness, won a third term in office against the opposition People's National Party (PNP). However, the JLP lost 14 seats to the PNP, still retaining a majority.

Q115328.label: Abelardo L. Rodríguez
Q115328.summary: Abelardo Rodríguez Luján, commonly known as Abelardo L. Rodríguez was a Mexican military officer, businessman and politician who served as Substitute President of Mexico from 1932 to 1934. He completed the term of President Pascual Ortiz Rubio after his resignation, during the period known as the Maximato, when Former President Plutarco Elías Calles held considerable de facto political power, without being president himself. Rodríguez was, however, more successful than Ortiz Rubio had been in asserting presidential power against Calles's influence.

Q887424.label: José Azcona del Hoyo
Q887424.summary: José Simón Azcona del Hoyo was President of Honduras from 27 January 1986 to 27 January 1990 for the Liberal Party of Honduras (PLH). He was born in La Ceiba in Honduras.

Q5174912.label: 1932 Costa Rican general election
Q5174912.desc: General election held in Costa Rica
Q5174912.summary: General elections were held in Costa Rica on 14 February 1932 to elect a president and half of the Constitutional Congress. Former president Ricardo Jiménez Oreamuno of the National Republican Party won a plurality of the presidential vote with 46.7%, ahead of Manuel Castro Quesada of the Republican Union, but failed to obtain the absolute majority required for election under the Constitution.

Q86682752.label: 2020 French Senate election
Q86682752.desc: senatorial election in France on September 27th, 2020
Q86682752.summary: Senatorial elections were held on 27 September 2020 to renew 172 of the 348 seats in the Senate of the French Fifth Republic. The elections were a modest victory for the centre-right Republicans.

Q1800832.label: 1981 Norwegian parliamentary election
Q1800832.desc: 1981 election for the parliament of Norway
Q1800832.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Norway on 13 and 14 September 1981. The elections led to the end of the Labour Party minority government and the creation of a Conservative Party minority government.

Q37933184.label: Hurricane Harvey
Q37933184.summary: Hurricane Harvey was a powerful and catastrophic tropical cyclone that made landfall in Texas and Louisiana in August 2017, causing widespread flooding and more than 100 deaths.

Q111144576.label: Battle of Irpin
Q111144576.img: Infrastructure of the University of the State Tax Service of Ukraine in Irpin damaged by Russian shelling.jpg
Q111144576.summary: As part of the Russian offensive on Kyiv during the Russian invasion of Ukraine, a battle took place for control of the city of Irpin. The combatants were elements of the Russian Armed Forces and Ukrainian Ground Forces. By 28 March 2022, Ukrainian forces recaptured the city.

Q114341504.label: September 2022 Burkina Faso coup d'état
Q114341504.desc: September 2022 coup to remove president Paul-Henri Sandaogo Damiba
Q114341504.summary: A coup d'état took place in Burkina Faso on 30 September 2022, removing Interim President Paul-Henri Sandaogo Damiba over his alleged inability to deal with the country's Islamist insurgency. Damiba had come to power in a coup d'état eight months earlier. Captain Ibrahim Traoré took over as interim leader.

Q3564160.label: Venizelism
Q3564160.summary: Venizelism was one of the major political movements in Greece beginning from the 1910s. The movement first formed under Eleftherios Venizelos in the 1910s and saw a resurgence of support in the 1960s when Georgios Papandreou united a coalition of old Venizelists and nationalist politicians.

Q2075264.label: Metaxism
Q2075264.desc: authoritarian nationalist ideology associated with Greek dictator Ioannis Metaxas
Q2075264.summary: Metaxism is a Greek authoritarian, fascist, ultra-nationalist, and monarchist ideology associated with Ioannis Metaxas. It called for the regeneration of the Greek nation and the establishment of a modern, culturally homogenous Greece. Metaxism disparaged liberalism, and held individual interests to be subordinate to those of the nation, seeking to mobilize the Greek people as a disciplined mass in service to the creation of a "new Greece."
